title: SQLite database layer with WAL mode and migrations
user_story: As an operator, I need Hookbin to create and manage its own SQLite database automatically so I never have to run migrations or set up a database manually.
description: Implement the Database struct wrapping a rusqlite Connection. On open: create the data directory if needed, open SQLite in WAL mode, enable foreign keys, run embedded migrations to create the hooks, requests, and tokens tables. Provide basic insert/query methods for the models. All errors are mapped to AppError. The database file lives at `{data_dir}/hookbin.db`.

acceptance_criteria.given: a data directory that does not exist
acceptance_criteria.then: the directory is created, hookbin.db is created, WAL mode is enabled, and the schema is applied

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing hookbin.db with the current schema
acceptance_criteria.then: migrations are idempotent — no error, no duplicate tables

acceptance_criteria.when: inserting a Hook and querying it back
acceptance_criteria.then: the Hook round-trips correctly with all fields preserved

acceptance_criteria.when: inserting a CapturedRequest and querying it back
acceptance_criteria.then: the CapturedRequest round-trips correctly including headers and body

acceptance_criteria.given: a database error (e.g., disk full simulation or constraint violation)
acceptance_criteria.then: the error is mapped to AppError::Internal with context, not a panic
tests use an in-memory SQLite database (`:memory:`) and verify schema creation, CRUD operations, WAL mode, and error mapping
